runners_data.name: Al Samsama
runners_data.note: Won on debut over this exact course and trip at Goodwood for Richard Hughes, with Ryan Moore booked — the class benchmark on ratings (OR 120) and the most natural front-runner in the field; 53 days off is the only mild query but everything else aligns for a bold show.

runners_data.name: China In Your Hand
runners_data.note: Three Goodwood runs all relevant — winner here over 7f and placed twice at the track — but her natural prominent style means she is likely to find herself shuffled further back than ideal in a field this loaded with pace, softening her prospects in scenarios where position is decisive.

runners_data.name: Sorrengail
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's filly steps up from 6f to 7f having won twice at Goodwood over shorter with Buick — the trip extension is the key question, but her course fluency and jockey partnership make her the standout beneficiary if she gets a prominent, covered berth just off the leaders.

runners_data.name: Spirit Tango
runners_data.note: Won over 6f at Sandown on her latest start for Ralph Beckett and Oisin Murphy, but both her runs at Goodwood have been over 6f and she now faces the step to 7f — the 62-day absence is worth noting, though Beckett's 8/41 in the last fortnight shows the yard is firing.

runners_data.name: The Can Can Queen
runners_data.note: Has genuine front-running credentials and a 6f Goodwood win to her name, but a patchy recent record including two poor efforts at this track and the step up to 7f for the first time are legitimate doubts; Callum Shepherd takes over and must judge whether to force or track.

runners_data.name: Global Success
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at 6f with five placed runs from seven starts, but a natural prominent racer who finds herself mapped to midfield by the congested pace picture — the blinkers are noted, and her OR of 66 leaves a significant class gap to bridge against the principals here.

races.paceDynamic: Al Samsama and The Can Can Queen are both confirmed front-runners, meaning this 7f Goodwood contest will be contested from the outset with neither horse likely to concede the lead without a fight. Al Samsama, trained by Richard Hughes and ridden by Ryan Moore, arrives on the back of a winning debut over this very course and trip and carries the higher class; The Can Can Queen, drawn wider and stepping up from 6f, will push hard to share or take the early gallop. The resulting pace should be honest rather than suicidal — two genuine pace-setters over 7f on Good ground at Goodwood typically produce an even, sustainable tempo that keeps the field compressed and makes the race honest throughout. This shape favours prominent racers who can sit just off a genuine lead and produce a sustained finish, rather than pure hold-up horses who need a truly end-to-end burn to get back into contention. Note that the field carries more front-running and prominent types than the shape can accommodate cleanly — Sorrengail and Spirit Tango are most likely to secure the premium prominent positions just off the two leaders, while China In Your Hand and Global Success, both naturally prominent in style, may find themselves shuffled wider or further back than they would choose.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Al Samsama and The Can Can Queen fight for the lead at a genuine but manageable tempo, handing the race to the horse travelling best just off the pace.
scenarios.body: The dual front-runners set an honest gallop that strings the field out, and a filly travelling smoothly in third or fourth emerges with a decisive turn of foot entering the Goodwood straight. Sorrengail's strong Goodwood form over shorter — two wins at the track — and William Buick's positional intelligence make her ideally placed to pounce, while Spirit Tango's sole win on a similar surface suggests she can sustain her effort.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Al Samsama Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Al Samsama is allowed to stride clear uncontested or The Can Can Queen fades quickly, leaving Ryan Moore to control the pace and steal an unassailable lead.
scenarios.body: Moore coaxes Al Samsama into a rhythm at a pace that is fast enough to be tactical but not so fierce that she empties, and no rival can close the gap from the two-furlong pole. Her debut win over this exact course and trip, combined with a trainer in Hughes who has hit 3/27 in the past 14 days, underlines her suitability for exactly this outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners burn each other out at a genuinely fierce early tempo, leaving the field ragged and opening a late lane for those ridden patiently.
scenarios.body: With both Al Samsama and The Can Can Queen refusing to back down, the leaders could hit a wall inside the final two furlongs and allow more conservatively ridden runners to emerge — though the redistribution of Global Success and China In Your Hand away from their natural prominent positions means neither is a true hold-up type capable of exploiting this fully. China In Your Hand's three-run Goodwood record and course familiarity at least gives her residual claims if this scenario develops.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy, No Clear Beneficiary
scenarios.trigger: If crowding, wayward running or soft patches in the draw disrupt the predicted race shape entirely, producing a messy contest with no horse able to dominate.
scenarios.body: A compressed, muddling gallop could see several runners race in unfamiliar positions with no one able to assert, flattening the form and throwing the contest open. In this scenario, the horse with the broadest adaptability and best finishing kick — regardless of preferred style — claims the spoils.

watchPoints.text: Al Samsama and The Can Can Queen — watch the first two furlongs to see which filly concedes the lead, as the outcome of that battle will define the tempo and the shape of the entire race.

Sorrengail — William Buick's positioning out of the gate is critical; if she gets shuffled back past midfield in the scramble for prominent spots, her winning chance diminishes sharply over a trip she has yet to prove.

China In Your Hand — despite strong Goodwood form, her natural style is prominent and she risks racing out of position from the start; monitor whether Paddy Bradley can carve out a forward berth or is swamped by the pace horses.

Spirit Tango — Oisin Murphy will have clear instructions given the 62-day break and the first run over 7f; watch whether she is ridden conservatively early or sent into the race, as that will signal trainer confidence in her fitness and stamina.

Global Success — the application of blinkers is worth tracking in the preliminaries; if she shows improved early energy, she may push further forward than her mapped position suggests, though her class deficit remains a significant hurdle.

races.name: Virgin Bet A Good Bet Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Jax Edge
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner with strong recent Goodwood course form and a 5f win here; uncontested lead is her optimal scenario, though she is racing slightly out of OR-profile at 78 and trainer form over 14 days is poor (0/6), which tempers confidence slightly.

runners_data.name: U S S Charleston
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type whose best form has come at 5f on similar ground (2nd at Goodwood), but simulated-going record is thin (5/15) and Luke Morris will need a stronger-than-expected pace to get competitive from the rear.

runners_data.name: Spring Bloom
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with excellent Goodwood form at 6f — stepping back to 5f is the query for this nine-year-old, though he has two wins and seven places at comparable trips and David Probert has strong course knowledge; trainer in solid 14-day form (2/19).

runners_data.name: Nogo's Dream
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride on this hold-up type, who has decent 5f Goodwood course form (2nd, 6th in recent visits) and wears headgear; Moore's ability to find a run in a compressed field is an asset, though the likely slow pace makes his natural style awkward.

runners_data.name: Independent Expert
runners_data.note: Aged seven with a lean recent form string (568946) and no wins from 15 similar-going runs; a genuine closer whose natural rearward role is squeezed by the volume of hold-up types, meaning he must race closer to the pace than he would choose — that constraint meaningfully reduces his chance.

runners_data.name: Over Spiced
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy picks up the ride on a mare whose course-and-distance form (2nd, 3rd twice at 5f Goodwood on good) is the most relevant in the field; a natural hold-up runner pushed into a midfield mapping by the crowded rear, she retains raw ability but needs the pace to be stronger than it looks likely to be.

runners_data.name: Kiss And Run
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with five recent runs at 5f on this track, placing three times; no wins in 15 similar-going runs is a concern, but Kieran O'Neill can keep her handy and she is well-drawn to take advantage if the leader weakens.

races.paceDynamic: Jax Edge is the one confirmed front runner here and, with no genuine rival likely to push for the lead from the off, she is set to control the pace through the five furlongs at Goodwood on good turf. Spring Bloom and Kiss And Run will press from prominent positions, providing a presence just off the pace without generating a true speed duel, meaning the overall tempo is likely to be steady-to-fair rather than scorching. The field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Independent Expert and Over Spiced are genuine closers who, squeezed out of their natural positions, are mapped to midfield and must be discounted as pure late-runners in this shape. This clean, uncontested lead for Jax Edge with a compressed mid-pack creates a race that favours horses racing prominently or travelling just off the pace, as the likely modest gallop will reward those who can sit close to the action and respond in the final furlong rather than those trying to come from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Clean Lead, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Jax Edge dictates a sustainable pace unchallenged and kicks off the home bend.
scenarios.body: Jax Edge controls every yard, the modest tempo suits a prominent handler, and she has recent Goodwood form at 5f on this ground; without a pace duel to expose her stamina, she is very hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just fast enough that Jax Edge ties up late and a close-tracking prominent horse collars her.
scenarios.body: Spring Bloom, who has a string of Goodwood form at 6f on good and has been placing consistently, is best placed to swoop; Kiss And Run also sits close enough to benefit if the leader fades inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finisher Comes Through
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a genuinely strong pace that opens up a gap for a horse tracking from mid-division.
scenarios.body: Over Spiced has excellent course form at 5f and consistent placing form in similar fields; though mapped to midfield out of her true hold-up role, she has the raw ability to capitalise if the pace is strong enough to create a gap.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closer Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpectedly hot pace strings the field out and leaves the rear horses with a clear run through.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given Jax Edge is uncontested and true closers Independent Expert and U S S Charleston would need a fast pace they are unlikely to get; U S S Charleston has placed at 5f on good going but would need everything to go wrong for the leaders.

watchPoints.text: Jax Edge will need to be tracked from the stalls — if she breaks cleanly and clears to the front unchallenged within the first furlong, she becomes the dominant threat given the likely modest pace.

Over Spiced, ridden by Oisin Murphy, may be asked to race closer than her natural style allows; watch for her position at the two-furlong marker — if she is travelling strongly in mid-division rather than off the pace, the race shape may be faster than it looks.

Spring Bloom at age nine stepping back from 6f to 5f is a distance query — if he travels comfortably in the early stages and is still going well turning for home, his consistent Goodwood form makes him a live threat to Jax Edge.

Ryan Moore on Nogo's Dream deserves monitoring — Moore tends to find positions that the raw form suggests are unavailable, and if he can tuck in just behind the leaders rather than being trapped in a true hold-up role, Nogo's Dream's 5f Goodwood placing form becomes more relevant.

The field is small (7 runners) and the rail draw at Goodwood's straight 5f is important — confirm draw positions at declarations as a low draw can be decisive in a small field on this track when pace is steady.

races.name: Virgin Bet Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Manxman
runners_data.note: Won over 16f at Goodwood last time out under Buick for the Crisfords and holds strong course form; a natural prominent racer who should slot in just behind Sax Appeal and will be well placed to quicken when the tempo lifts in the straight — headgear (visor) worn.

runners_data.name: Synergism
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's four-year-old has a win at Goodwood over 14f and returns from 46 days off, which Prescott routinely manages well; sits prominently in his natural style and this step to 2m should suit a horse bred and trained to stay, with the Good going ideal.

runners_data.name: Bahadur
runners_data.note: Has a win at 16f on Good ground but recent form has been patchy with several poor runs; genuinely wants to race prominently but the presence of Manxman and Synergism means he is unlikely to secure his preferred spot, and the style compromise reduces his winning prospects materially in this shape.

runners_data.name: Fireblade
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne's hold-up mount has placed four times at Goodwood including twice in this class over shorter trips; the big question is whether the step to 2m and a modest pace from Sax Appeal gives her enough late sectionals to close — she needs genuine gallop to deliver her finish.

runners_data.name: Sax Appeal
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's six-year-old has been consistently placed but winless in six runs, setting pace or tracking it throughout; uncontested lead here suits his profile perfectly and he could prove hard to pass if he jumps well and controls the fractions, though his record of 0W1P in similar going is noted.

races.paceDynamic: Sax Appeal is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of five and will set sail from the gates over this 2m trip on Good ground at Goodwood, creating a measured, uncontested gallop that is unlikely to be pressured from any rival. Manxman and Synergism are both prominent types who will track Sax Appeal through the early stages, giving the race a settled, single-file shape with a small field unlikely to generate genuine pace pressure at any point. Fireblade is the one confirmed hold-up horse and will be ridden from behind this dawdling-to-honest tempo, needing a strong late move up the Goodwood straight to get competitive. The field contains more prominent-profile horses than can all sit in their natural position — Bahadur, a genuine prominent type, is redistributed to midfield in the map because Manxman and Synergism are better placed to occupy that tracking berth — meaning the race shape most strongly favours horses who can sit close to the pace and quicken from a forward position when Sax Appeal's lead begins to compress in the final quarter-mile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Close Finishers
scenarios.trigger: If Sax Appeal dictates an honest but uncontested gallop and the prominent trackers Manxman and Synergism sit poised to strike two out.
scenarios.body: Sax Appeal sets the terms throughout, and with no rival applying pressure the pace will be fair rather than searching, compressing the finish into a sprint from the two-furlong pole up the hill; horses who have tracked the pace throughout are best positioned to respond to that acceleration.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Sax Appeal quickens from the front early in the straight and the prominent chasers are caught flat-footed or unable to accelerate.
scenarios.body: With a small field and no serious challenger, Sax Appeal could steal a race-winning advantage before the home turn and simply outstay the field up Goodwood's long straight; this suits a horse comfortable making the running at a comfortable clip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Burst Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and Fireblade's hold-up style delivers a powerful late run.
scenarios.body: Fireblade has placed twice in this sort of company at Goodwood over shorter but is stepping up significantly in trip, and a genuine pace would allow her to close ground in the final furlong; the concern is that Sax Appeal's tempo may not be strong enough to set up this scenario with only five runners.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Sax Appeal goes too slow, creating a false pace that causes a bunched finish with multiple horses challenging simultaneously.
scenarios.body: In a five-runner field with Good ground and a modest gallop, the race could turn into a tactical sprint from the three-furlong mark, favouring horses with a sharp turn of foot rather than true stamina; Bahadur, though likely racing in a role not fully suited to its redistribution, could sneak into contention if the race becomes uncharacteristically messy.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Manxman under William Buick moves up to press Sax Appeal early — if Buick elects to sit right on the leader's quarters rather than leave a gap, it could accelerate the tempo and dramatically change who benefits in the straight.
Synergism's 46-day absence is worth monitoring in the paddock; Prescott horses are usually fit fresh but any signs of a big handicap mark on return could see him drop away before the final turn.

Bahadur's redistribution to midfield means Cieren Fallon will face a tactical decision early — if he pushes forward against his mapped position and traffic develops in a five-runner field, it could interfere with Manxman or Synergism's rhythm.

Fireblade's recent Goodwood form shows she handles the track, but her best runs have come over shorter; watch her position at the top of the straight — if she is still more than three lengths off the pace entering the final two furlongs, the trip may simply not play to her hold-up style.

Sax Appeal has not won in six runs but has finished third four times; if he repeats that pattern and ties up close home, the winner is almost certainly Manxman or Synergism depending on which has tracked more economically.

races.name: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Oasis Sunrise
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a strong Goodwood record — two wins and multiple placings at this course over this exact 1m2f trip — and Cieren Fallon's course knowledge makes this a serious contender to track Boy George and land a late challenge; sim-going figures are solid and 11 days since last run is no concern.

runners_data.name: Sir Edward Lear
runners_data.note: Consistently prominent, has placed four times at Goodwood including recent course runs over this trip, and George Wood will be keen to hold a stalking position; headgear note (p) suggests he needs confidence and a clean passage, and his last two runs at the track are encouraging.

runners_data.name: Hello Cotai
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse by nature, but two Goodwood wins at 10f and a recent course run show this track genuinely suits; Pat Cosgrave knows the course well, though the distance is slightly longer than recent wins and she will need the pace to set up a late run.

runners_data.name: Blue Wonder
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has been off 87 days, a notable absence, and has only one placing on Good ground from five attempts in similar conditions; Oisin Murphy adds significant riding quality but this horse needs things to fall right from the rear and the absence is a red flag.

runners_data.name: Boy George
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with an exceptional three-race winning sequence at Goodwood over this exact course and distance; the 441-day absence is the critical unknown, and Dominic Ffrench Davis has a blank record (0/7) over 14 days, but if fit he controls this race's shape entirely.

runners_data.name: Lady McC
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a tongue tie and a 131-day layoff, carrying a poor Goodwood record of two unplaced runs at the track; Paddy Bradley rides and the form string shows no win or placing on Good ground in six attempts, making this a very difficult profile.

runners_data.name: Decalogue
runners_data.note: Hold-up type stepping up to 1m2f from recent 7-8f assignments, and trainer Jamie Osborne has form (4/16 over 14 days); Saffie Osborne takes the ride, but the horse is only 3yo and ran just five days ago, which is a fitness positive but the trip extension is unproven.

runners_data.name: Prodigal Son
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose natural position is off the pace, here placed in the midfield map because the field is saturated with closers — Luke Morris will struggle to find a clear run if the field settles in a bunch; recent form shows one placing from six runs, and blinkers are fitted.

runners_data.name: Connie Moon
runners_data.note: A hold-up type by preference, shifted to a midfield slot on the map as true rear-runners are oversubscribed in this field; has a visor fitted and a winless recent sequence, with limited form on Good ground (one placing from ten) and a Goodwood record of just one placing.

runners_data.name: Platinum Prince
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who naturally races from hold-up, represented in midfield on the map only because of the rear-runner surplus; blinkers fitted and a sparse record of one win and one place from fifteen runs on similar going, and Toby Moore (7lb claimer) can help the weight but the profile is modest.

runners_data.name: Benavente
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner who finished second in a 12f Stall race recently and has placed at 10f too; Finley Marsh takes the ride for a trainer with limited Goodwood form (1/15 on similar going), and the horse drops to 131lbs which helps, though his Goodwood record includes a 10th over 6f — the trip extension is the key positive here.

runners_data.name: Brave Leader
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up horse whose true rear-running preference means the midfield map position overstates his likely tactical position; David Probert is a quality booking and the horse has placed over 12f on soft, but no wins in the form string and a blank Goodwood record make this a tough ask.

races.paceDynamic: Boy George is the lone confirmed front-runner here, returning from 441 days off but with a striking record of three consecutive wins at Goodwood over this course and distance, and he will stride to the front unchallenged from the outset. With no rival willing or able to match him for the lead, he will control every fraction on Good ground that suits him, ensuring a measured, sustainable gallop rather than a searching test. The prominent racers — Oasis Sunrise, Sir Edwards Lear, and Benavente — will need to track him and will be best placed to capitalise should he weaken, while the cluster of hold-up horses will face a stiff task if fractions are not truly testing. This race shape — one unchallenged leader setting a comfortable pace — heavily favours horses racing prominently or from just off the pace, particularly those with a proven record at Goodwood; hold-up horses are structurally disadvantaged unless the gallop quickens significantly in the straight. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the map can place at the rear, with Prodigal Son, Connie Moon, Platinum Prince, and Brave Leader redistributed to midfield — of the true prominent horses, Oasis Sunrise and Sir Edward Lear are most likely to secure natural positions just behind Boy George.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Boy George Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Boy George jumps cleanly and dictates an uncontested, measured gallop from the front.
scenarios.body: Boy George sets his own fractions on familiar Goodwood ground, conserving energy through the long bend, and his three recent wins here over this exact trip suggest the track suits him uniquely; a horse returning fit from a long absence but with proven course form could simply be too good for rivals who never see him. Oasis Sunrise and Sir Edward Lear, tracking just off the pace, are the chief dangers if Boy George idles or weakens entering the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Reels Him In
scenarios.trigger: If Boy George sets a slightly too-generous gallop in the middle stages and one of the tracking horses collars him inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Oasis Sunrise has strong course form over this trip at Goodwood with two wins and multiple placings at the track, and Cieren Fallon will be perfectly positioned to pounce if the leader's stride shortens; Sir Edward Lear similarly has Goodwood form and George Wood can time a challenge from a close-up position. This is the most likely alternative shape, as genuine prominent types find natural berths just behind the leader and need only a fractional error from Boy George.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Surprises Field
scenarios.trigger: If Boy George sets a genuinely strong gallop that burns off the prominent horses and leaves the race truly open for closers in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Hello Cotai has won twice at Goodwood and has recent course form, so if the hold-up trip suits she can run on powerfully; Blue Wonder with Oisin Murphy aboard is another who could emerge from midfield if the pace genuinely tests the leaders. However, this scenario requires a faster early tempo than Boy George's lone-leader scenario typically generates, making it the least probable outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Pace, Pack Arrives Together
scenarios.trigger: If Boy George is pressured unexpectedly early by an eager prominent horse and the resulting uneven gallop bunches the field for a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A scrambled finish plays into the hands of whoever gets the clearest run through, and Hello Cotai's proven ability to quicken at Goodwood gives her an edge; Decalogue, stepping up in trip from recent 8f form, could also benefit if the race becomes a test of finishing speed rather than stamina. This scenario depends on unlikely pressure being applied to the leader and is low-probability given the docile pace map.

watchPoints.text: Boy George's 441-day absence is the single biggest swing factor in this race — if he returns fully tuned he dictates entirely, but if ring-rusty he could fold turning in and hand the race to Oasis Sunrise or Sir Edward Lear at a stroke.

Oasis Sunrise and Sir Edward Lear may both attempt to track Boy George prominently, creating a potential positional battle between them in the early stages that could disrupt either runner's rhythm approaching the Goodwood bend.

Hello Cotai ran only 8 days ago and steps up markedly in trip to 1m2f; Pat Cosgrave will need to manage her energy carefully from the hold-up position, and any signs of a slowly-run early pace will make her task harder.

Blue Wonder's 87-day absence and a single placing from ten runs on Good or similar ground means Oisin Murphy may struggle to get him competitive despite the rider quality — monitor his market moves for any strong stable confidence signals.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Prodigal Son, Connie Moon, Platinum Prince, Brave Leader — will all be competing for the same ground in the straight; with a slowly-run race likely, traffic is a genuine risk for any of them attempting to quicken through a packed field.

races.name: Virgin Bet Daily Price Boosts Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mister Bluebird
runners_data.note: Confirmed lone front-runner who sets his own fractions; wears a hood, trained by Heather Main, and ran just 10 days ago — freshness fine; five-time runner at Goodwood with two placings at 7f here, dropping to 6f suits his galloping style; sim-going record modest (0 wins) but Good conditions present no issue.

runners_data.name: Marengo Storm
runners_data.note: Progressive three-year-old with two wins at Goodwood including over this course and distance, making him the most course-confident challenger; Richard Hughes yard in fair form (T14: 3/27); 38 days since last run but showed no signs of going stale last season; best placed if he can sit just off Mister Bluebird's shoulder.

runners_data.name: Old Is Gold
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy booked for Andrew Balding's consistent three-year-old who has run eight times at Goodwood with solid course form; primarily a 5f horse stepping to 6f again where he was placed last time on soft; the visor is retained and the Good ground suits, though he may find the extra furlong searching.

runners_data.name: Atticum
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell hold-up three-year-old who recorded back-to-back thirds at Goodwood over 5f; stepping up to 6f for the first time in handicap company; Marco Ghiani takes the ride; 41 days off the track, and his entire sim-going form has come without a win (0W/2P) — needs things to pan out in front of him.

runners_data.name: Arry Up
runners_data.note: Prominently-raced three-year-old with a win at Goodwood over 5f last time at the track; Lewis Edmunds claiming; recent form includes a distant 19th at Goodwood which is a concern, but prior to that has shown genuine pace; likely to push for the position just off Mister Bluebird early.

runners_data.name: Brosay
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type with a dismal recent sequence (three nines and a ten in last four) and trainer Charlie Pike without a winner in the last seven runners (T14: 0/7); visor retained but blinkers may be an issue; Good ground is not a concern but recent efforts at Goodwood suggest he is running below his best.

runners_data.name: An Outlaw's Grace
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's four-year-old is a natural hold-up performer who has placed five times in 15 runs on similar ground without a win; because the field carries too many true closers for the map to place them all at the rear, this horse is shown in midfield — it will not be racing from its preferred berth, and that positional compromise tempers confidence in its chance.

runners_data.name: Born Slippy
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old wearing a tongue tie; last run 41 days ago and latest form figures at Goodwood include a 25th — the worst effort in the field; Richard Spencer yard in modest recent form (T14: 2/9); two placed runs on softer ground but the proximity of that 25th at this very track is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Evie Ross
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's three-year-old wears a visor and has a consistent midfield record at Goodwood (five runs here with a best of 5th); a genuine hold-up type whose natural race position is off the back of the field — in this pace-light shape, she is shifted forward on the map but that does not reflect how Probert is likely to ride her, reducing the probability that she meaningfully influences the outcome.

races.paceDynamic: Mister Bluebird is the lone confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 6f handicap and, with no genuine rival likely to contest the lead aggressively, he should be able to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop from the gates. Marengo Storm and Arry Up will push forward to dispute the prominent slots just behind him, but neither is likely to put Mister Bluebird under meaningful early pressure. The redistributed hold-up types — An Outlaw's Grace and Evie Ross — are true closers who will be squeezed into midfield positions rather than their natural rear berths, meaning the backmarker end of the field is less deeply stacked than it appears on the map. A controlled pace set by a lone front-runner on Good turf over 6f at Goodwood — a track that does not inherently punish leaders — strongly favours horses racing prominently or tracking close to the pace, with the ability to assert from 2f out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mister Bluebird Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Mister Bluebird is allowed to stride clear unchallenged early and the prominent horses behind cannot close the gap from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Mister Bluebird dictates a comfortable gallop, never fully extending himself until challenged in the final furlong, and his rivals simply cannot get to him on Good ground; horses who pressed forward early and conserved energy behind the leader are best placed to fill the frame.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Marengo Storm or Arry Up press up closer than expected mid-race and have enough left to collar Mister Bluebird inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The early pace proves just sustainable enough to keep the front-runner honest, allowing a horse travelling prominently in second or third to sustain a run and wear Mister Bluebird down near the line; the Good going rewards a horse with a good Goodwood record tracking a true pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and Mister Bluebird sets a tempo that burns out the prominent brigade, leaving a gap for a horse coming from behind.
scenarios.body: Atticum or Born Slippy, racing in genuine midfield, could pick up the pieces if front-runners tie each other up; however, this scenario is structurally less likely given the absence of a pace pressurer and the presence of redistributed hold-up horses who will not truly be hunting from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches — Draw Plays
scenarios.trigger: If a slow early tempo causes the entire field to compress and the race is decided by a sprint finish from 2f out.
scenarios.body: With nine runners on Good Goodwood turf and no pace battle, a dawdle-and-sprint finish could randomise the result, benefiting horses that accelerate well in a bunched dash; this is the least likely shape given Mister Bluebird's tendency to roll along regardless.

watchPoints.text: Mister Bluebird goes unchallenged in front — if Cieren Fallon is given a completely uncontested lead, the lack of pressure could make him very hard to run down over a track that does not inherently punish front-runners.

Marengo Storm's course form is the strongest in the field (wins at 6f and 7f here at Goodwood) — watch to see if Finley Marsh positions him within striking range of the leader from the off, as that would significantly heighten his threat.

An Outlaw's Grace and Evie Ross are true hold-up horses forced into a more forward map position — if either is ridden patiently from the rear as expected, they will be giving ground to the pace and may struggle to close on a controlled gallop.

Old Is Gold steps back up from 5f to 6f with Oisin Murphy — the class of the jockey booking on a horse with strong course form is worth noting, but watch whether he can quicken adequately over the extra furlong on Good ground.
Brosay's trainer Charlie Pike has recorded zero wins from nine runners in the last 14 days — a cold yard flag that adds context to already-poor recent form figures for this horse at Goodwood.
